M.L. SAHNI, MEMBER
1. M/s Air India Ltd.-the
OP before the District Forum, have filed this appeal challenging Forums
order dated 04.06.2008 whereby the OP
(hereinafter referred to as the Appellant)
have been directed to pay to the Respondent (complainant) Rs. 87,667/- the price of the ticket , Rs.
1,00,000/- towards compensation for causing mental agony and harassment and Rs. 10,000/- towards cost of litigation, on variety of
grounds , inter alia,
that the father of the complainant
did not have proper authorization to file the consumer complaint and
that the District Forum awarded and exorbitant amount of Rs.
1,00,000/- towards compensation as against prayer of the complaint asking for Rs. 50,000/- for mental agony and harassment.
2. Briefly stated the facts of the case,
are that Respondent had booked return ticket from New
 York to Delhi for 26.01.2001 and
from Delhi to New York vide flight No. AI-III for 04.03.2001 via London with the
Appellant/OP under a highly concessional scheme from
its agent at United States.
The said ticket under the excursion fare was inter-alia
non-refundable and non-endorsable as was clearly mentioned on the ticket
itself. The complainant/respondent
utilized the aforementioned ticket for one side and arrived in India on
26.01.2001.
3. According to the Appellant, Respondent through its agent
Mr. Anwar approached the tele-reservation
facility of the Appellant/OP and requested for postponement of the confirmed
ticket of return flight to New York
dated 04.03.2001 to 11.03.200. In view
of above request, the Appellant entered the details in its computer system and
a separate PNR number was generated for reservation on 11.03.2001. As a matter of policy and business prudence,
two bookings against the name of one person cannot be left open, therefore, the
system is made to provide a time frame within which the passenger has to decide
his option. The system for reservation granted a time limit on 13.02.2001 for
confirmation of date of the return flight and the same was communicated
instantly to the agent of the complainant/respondent. In view of non-confirmation, the ticket could
not have been left open endlessly and hence the system automatically cancelled
the entire PNR of the Respondent/complainant on the basis of expiry of time
limit. Respondent approached the
Appellant on 03.03.2001 for purchase of fresh ticket in the same flight i.e.
AI-111 for 04.03.2001. Due to peak season, the ticket of economy class was not
available in the flight in question and the same was conveyed to the Respondent
personally. Since no seat was available
in the economy class and keeping in view the urgency of the Respondent, he was
informed that the seats are only available in J-class category and if he wishes
he could avail the same. The Respondent opted for J-class ticket and the same
was made available to him on due payment.
4. Conversely, the case of the Respondent, as per his sworn
testimony filed before the Ld. District Forum in the form of Affidavit was that
he had not authorized Mr. Anwar for making request
for postponing of the confirmed O.K. Status ticket of the flight from
04.03.2001 to 11.03.2001. He had requested M/s South End Travel, New Delhi to enquire from Air India Authorities about the
position of booking for 11.3.2001 for New York
( USA).
On enquiring on telephone from Air India Reservation Representative for Air
India Flight IA -111 to New York,
the Representative of Air India Authorities intimated that there is no
possibility for 11.03.2001. He did not
know the alleged Shri Anwar
and he did not authorize anybody for postponement/ cancellation of the
confirmed O.K. Status ticket for 4.3.2001.
5. We
have heard the Ld. Counsel for the parties and have examined the impugned order
passed by the District forum, New
 Delhi (KG Marg).
6. It
shall not be in-apposite to recall the observations of this Commission, make on
25.09.2008, while admitting this appeal. The same are extracted below :
In view of the contention of the counsel
for the appellant that respondent had asked for compensation of Rs. 50,000/- besides refund of ticket amount on account of
wrongful cancellation of the ticket but the District Forum has acted to obverboard that it directed the appellant not only to pay
the price of the tickets amounting to Rs. 87,667/-
but also compensation of Rs. 1,00,000/- and Rs. 10,000/- as cost of litigation, if it is so, the
District Forum has exceeded its brief and the impugned order reflects utter
non-application of mind and element of whimsicality and capriciousness.
Protection of rights of consumer does not mean enriching the consumer unjustly.
He has to be compensated reasonably for mental agony and harassment or actual
loss. It appears that the District Forum is not adhering to the guidelines and observations made by this Commission as almost in every case
compensation is being awarded in lacs whereas
the actual loss suffered by the consumer runs into few thousands.
5. Holding
the Appellant guilty of unfair trade practice and for deficiency-in-service,
the Ld. District Forum have recorded in its findings that time limits are set for purchase of tickets and not for getting
confirmed reservation. Assuming, what Air India states can be given credence,
then, Air India should itself have a contacted the complainant on 13.2.2001 and
told him that seat would not be available to him on 11.3.2001, whether he would
like to travel on 4.3.2001 for which he had confirmed booking. It is clear that
the booking for 4.3.2001 was cancelled on 14.2.1001 at 7.17 hours without
notice and consent of the complainant. The system ought not to have removed the
booking for 4.3.2001 without the consent of the complainant. There is nothing
on record to show that the complainant had authorized Air India to cancel the reservation.
Having erroneously and recklessly cancelled the booking of the complainant for
4.3.2001 the Air India
provides seat in the same flight by charging Rs.
80,667/- without giving the credit of the cost of the ticket held by the
complainant.
6. Considering
the affidavit of the complainant filed before the Ld. District Forum there
appears to us no fault in the findings recorded by the Ld. District Forum, as
cited above. However, we agree with the Ld. Counsel for the Appellant that
award of the compensation in the form damages is highly unjustified and irrational in the given facts
and circumstance of the case. The respondents stands
fully compensated when the refund of the price of the ticket paid by him in
lieu of the alleged wrong cancellation of his confirming Ticket for 4.3.2001 is
ordered. The appellants are not liable to be doubly penalized, especially when
the alleged confirmed booking of return flight was a highly concessional
excursion ticket issued under highly concessional
scheme in United States having restrictions attached to it as stated in exhibit
filed alongwith the affidavit of Shri M.B. Loker,
Commercial Manager, NI of the Appellant before the Ld. District Forum in their
evidence and which fact was not discussed by the Respondent (complainant).
7. We
are, therefore, of the considered view that the impugned order is liable to be
modified to the extent that compensation of Rs. 1,00,000/- awarded in this case is un-warranted. Hence,
allowing the appeal partly , it is directed that the
Respondent shall be refunded Rs. 80,667/- the price
of the ticket purchased by him for
undertaking the return journey from USA with cost of litigation of Rs. 10,000/- , as awarded by the Ld. District Forum, within
30 days from the receipt of this order by the Appellant , failing which they
shall be liable to pay interest @ 9% p.a. on the above stated amount till
realization.
8. FDR,
if any , deposited by the appellant, be released after completion of due
formalities.
9. Copy
of this order be provided free of cost to the parties, as per statutory
requirement. Copy of this order be sent to the
concerned District Forum and thereafter the file be consigned to record room.
(JUSTICE BARKAT ALI ZAIDI)
